title: lnd admin REST API bound to 0.0.0.0 in the wireguard preset; host firewall is the only protection layer
evidence: services.lnd.restAddress = "0.0.0.0" with tor.enforce = false when lndconnect is enabled. The macaroon-admin REST API is reachable on all interfaces; protection is the nixos-fw default-drop plus an accept rule scoped to -i wg-nb from the single peer /32. Assertions refuse a disabled firewall and the nftables backend; restrictPeer REJECT is inserted at chain top.
impact: Any firewall bypass, rule regression, or future NixOS firewall semantics change exposes a wallet-admin API to the LAN/WAN. Defense-in-depth is single-layer.
recommendation: Work through docs/wireguard-rest-bind.md (systemd ordering, TLS SAN, ExecStartPost/btcpayserver/lndconnect-onion consumers) and bind to the wg address; until then keep the documented advisory.

title: Operator user is root-equivalent by design (full bitcoind RPC, lnd admin macaroon, NOPASSWD run-as)
status: known-documented (upstream model, warning comments in tree)
evidence: operator is in group bitcoin and reads the privileged RPC cookie (postStart chmod 0640, warning comment audit L-10); operator is in the lnd group and can read admin.macaroon; doas/sudo NOPASSWD to the lnd user.
impact: Compromise of the operator account equals compromise of funds and the node. Anyone deploying must treat operator SSH keys as root-equivalent.
recommendation: Keep documenting; optionally split operator into a read-only role and a funds-admin role if the fleet ever needs it.

title: CVE whitelist blanket-pname entries silence all future CVEs for build-toolchain packages if they ever enter the runtime closure
status: known-accepted (own comment: revisit if a service runs one at runtime)
evidence: [gcc], [go], [cargo], [binutils], [ninja], [patch], [ada] (and peers) whitelist every current and future CVE for those pnames. The scan target is the node toplevel runtime closure, so the entries should stay inert; if a runtime closure ever legitimately includes one, its CVEs are silently ignored.
impact: A future closure change could make a real attack-surface CVE invisible to the weekly scan with no signal.
recommendation: Have cve-scan.sh fail or warn when a blanket-whitelisted pname actually appears in the scanned closure.

title: CalVer release tags are created unsigned by CI
evidence: release-tag.yml runs as github-actions[bot] with contents:write and pushes annotated tags with no signing. SECURITY.md states a tag is a convenience pointer, commits are SSH-signed, and instructs pinning by commit + narHash.
impact: A compromised CI token could retarget a tag; flake users are bound by flake.lock narHash, but tag-name consumers (github:.../release) would silently track the moved pointer.
recommendation: Sign tags with the maintainer SSH key, or have the workflow verify the pushed commit's SSH signature before tagging.

title: Branch-protection ruleset and GitHub-side signature verification are asserted in comments but unverifiable from the checkout
evidence: The trust story ('release branch ruleset only accepts commits with all CI checks green', 'commits are shown as Verified') depends on GitHub-side configuration outside the repo tree.
impact: A repo-only audit cannot confirm those controls exist.
recommendation: Consumers should verify branch protection and commit signatures on GitHub before trusting the release branch.

title: MemoryDenyWriteExecute disabled for btcpayserver and nbxplorer (.NET JIT)
evidence: MemoryDenyWriteExecute = false for both .NET services; remainder of defaultHardening, netns/Tor policy, and dedicated users unchanged.
impact: W^X enforcement absent on the largest web-facing parsing surface on the node.
recommendation: Re-check whether .NET supports W^X-compatible JIT modes on current runtimes.

title: No backdoor, exfiltration, or supply-chain compromise indicators found in the fork-specific changes
evidence: All 70 fork commits reviewed; full diff from upstream base 37931e5 examined. All fetches HTTPS + hash-pinned from official sources; netns-exec whitelisted to live netns, requires absolute path, drops caps; every fix claimed in docs/security-audit-2026-08-14.md and the 2026-08/09 hardening commits is present in the tree and pinned by VM tests (macaroon symlink canary, wg tunnel reachability, nbxplorer inotify count); CI actions SHA-pinned; cve-scan fail-closed; fork pins itself (not upstream) in all examples.
impact: The fork behaves as its README claims: a trimmed, actively hardened continuation, not a trojaned fork.
recommendation: None. Re-audit on every nixpkgs pin bump as the project itself prescribes.
